subject: History
name: Basic 6 History
description: The Basic 6 History curriculum focuses on the impact of European presence, political developments under colonial rule, the formation of political parties, the journey to independence, the Republics, and military rule in Ghana.

strands.title: Europeans in Ghana
strands.description: Assessing the impact of European presence.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of the impact of European presence on Ghana

indicators.description: Assess the changes that the European presence brought to Ghana.

exemplars.description: Show and discuss a documentary of European presence in Ghana.
Discuss the activities the Europeans engaged in (trade, vocational training centres, health facilities, development of local alphabet, translation of the Bible).
Debate the impacts of European presence on Ghana.

strands.title: Colonisation and Developments under Colonial Rule in Ghana

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of Political developments under colonial rule, 1874-1957.

indicators.description: Describe the features of British colonial rule in Ghana including 'direct' and 'indirect' rule, 1874-1957.

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts of 'direct' and 'indirect' rule.
Discuss the features of 'direct' and 'indirect' rule.
Discuss the division of the colony into provinces.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of 'direct' and 'indirect' rule.
Role play indirect rule in the Gold Coast.

strands.title: Journey to Independence
strands.description: Political parties and the path to independence.

subStrands.title: Formation of Political Parties
subStrands.description: Role of political parties in the independence struggle.

contentStandards.description: Appreciate the role played by the leadership of political parties in the struggle for independence from 1947 to 1957

indicators.description: Describe the role played by the leaders of the two major political parties (UGCC and CPP) in the independence struggle in the Gold Coast after the Second World War.

exemplars.description: Define a political party.
Discuss the formation of the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) in 1947.
Discuss the formation of the Convention People Party (CPP) in 1949.
Discuss the role played by the leaders of the UGCC and CPP in the struggle for independence.
Learners map out specific roles by leaders such as Kwame Nkrumah, J.B. Danquah, Obetsebi Lamptey, Ako Adjei, William Ofori Atta and Edward Akuffo Addo.
Learners explain how these leaders became known as 'the Big Six'.
Show and discuss a documentary on the independence eve rally by the CPP.
Learners recount an Independence Day celebration in their community.
Enact the declaration of independence by Kwame Nkrumah.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the course of events leading to independence from 1948 to 1957

indicators.description: Explain post World War II developments in the Gold Coast

exemplars.description: Discuss the establishment of the Watson Commission.
Report on the findings of the Commission in the form of a paper or performance/poster/role play etc.
Recount lessons learnt from the Watson Commission's report, e.g. recommendation to set up the Coussey Committee to review the constitution of the Gold Coast.
Discuss the main recommendation in the Coussey committee report.

indicators.description: Explain how Ghana gained independence through constitutional means.

exemplars.description: Discuss the first general elections held in 1951.
Use a resource person (retired educationalist, veteran soldier, retired police officer, senior citizens etc.) to discuss the sequence of events leading to the 1956 elections.
Discuss the outcome of the 1956 elections.
Enact a scene of an election at a polling station.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of the Fourth Republic (1992 to date).

indicators.description: Describe the events leading to the emergence of the Fourth Republic.

exemplars.description: Describe the process leading to the emergence of the Fourth Republic (e.g. drawing of a new constitution, referendum, lifting of the ban on political parties, general elections of 1992 etc.).
List the names of all the Presidents of the Fourth Republics and their dates of tenure.
Learners use internet to find out some biographical details (name, date of birth, place of birth, family, educational backgrounds, hobbies etc.) about presidents of the Fourth Republic of Ghana.
Show and discuss a documentary on the inauguration of a new President of Ghana.
Learners recount an inauguration they have witnessed or seen on Television.
Discuss other key figures in the Fourth Republic (e.g. Chief Justices, Speakers of Parliament, Vice Presidents etc.).

indicators.description: Identify the political parties that have governed the country under the Fourth Republic

exemplars.description: Identify the governments that have so far handed over power peacefully through an election.
List the parties and their dates of tenure in office in the Fourth Republic.
Use the internet/resource persons/documentaries/visits to district/municipal assemblies to identify achievements of various governments within their respective districts.
Learners discuss their findings in class.

contentStandards.description: Understand that military takeovers interrupted constitutional rule on four occasions since 1966, with some consequences.

indicators.description: Identify the leaders of the coup d'états and names of their regimes.

exemplars.description: List the military regimes since 1966 and their leaders.
Show and discuss a documentary on any of the military take overs.

indicators.description: Assess the consequences of military takeovers on Ghana's development

exemplars.description: Show and discuss a documentary of any military takeover.
Brainstorm the effects of the coup d'états and military rule on Ghana's development (e.g. human right abuse, overthrow of constitutions and imposition of harsh rules).
Debate the effects of military takeovers on Ghana's development.
